Many organizations still rely solely on having an active SSL certificate, overlooking critical transport headers and TCP socket exposure that leave web perimeters vulnerable under OWASP guidelines. I engineered this platform using Next.js (App Router), TypeScript, and Node.js network sockets, solving core security and networking challenges: 🔒 Strict Anti-SSRF Defense: Deterministic filtering of RFC 1918 private ranges and loopback interfaces to prevent backend proxy misuse. ⚡ Socket Timeouts & Redirect Handling: Enforcing manual redirect inspection and AbortSignal timeouts to prevent process blocking from hanging ports.

articles.title: Label Promise.any() inputs so AggregateError.errors drive retries not mysteries
articles.excerpt: If you race multiple mirrors, caches, or endpoints with Promise.any(), the all-fail case often trips teams: the catch block receives an AggregateError and the code treats the failure as a single anony…
articles.body: If you race multiple mirrors, caches, or endpoints with Promise.any(), the all-fail case often trips teams: the catch block receives an AggregateError and the code treats the failure as a single anonymous incident. Promise.any() actually gives you what you need to make that failure actionable: an AggregateError whose errors array preserves the input order. Implementation approach (no code here — the server will insert the verified example): label each source before you pass it into Promise.any(). Convert rejections into Error objects that carry a stable sourceLabel and the originalReason. When Promise.any() rejects, inspect aggregate.errors in input order and classify each entry with a predicate that answers “retryable or fatal?”.

Disclosure: we build Opti-Behavior, the plugin mentioned in some sections. If your WooCommerce checkout is not working, the cause is almost always one of five things: a JavaScript error on the checkout page, a plugin or theme conflict, a cached checkout page, a payment gateway problem, or a broken HTTPS or session setup. This guide shows the signs, then 9 checks to run in order, most of them without any extra plugin, and how to confirm the fix on your live store. articles.excerpt: Anakin Skywalker actor Hayden Christensen has revealed the strangest fan encounter he’s ever had.
articles.body: Anakin Skywalker actor Hayden Christensen has revealed the strangest fan encounter he’s ever had. Speaking on stage at L.A. Comic Con, as reported by The Nerd Wire , the Star Wars veteran said that years ago, a burglar recognized him during a robbery at his home, apologized, then gave his stuff back. Christensen was upstairs when he heard the door open, and when he found the burglar, he was holding his belongings. “I’m like, is this a delivery guy?” Christensen was quoted as saying. “And I look and I’m like, this is all my stuff.” Remarkably, Christensen then offered to buy the man who broke into his house a train ticket home. No, a Jedi mind trick hadn’t caused the burglar to have a surprise change of heart. He just happened to be a fan who decided on a quick U-turn.

articles.body: On Episode 234 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Mike Wall are joined by Than Putzig of the Planetary Science Institute about a NASA-backed payload bound for the Marius Hills Pit on the moon. In our ongoing quest to develop a moon base, could we possibly utilize the area beneath the surface of the moon in order to make the moon habitable? Could Marius Hills Pit, a roughly 50-meter-wide opening that may lead into a lunar lava tube, become the Moon's first living habitat for humans? Putzig explains how geophysical instruments on a rover could detect hidden voids beneath the surface and measure the size of these lava tubes.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 31, 2015: Creepy skull-shaped Halloween asteroid flies by Earth, NASA names it the 'Great Pumpkin'
articles.excerpt: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. Here's why it was so creepy.
articles.body: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. It arrived with excellent timing on Halloween, which made the already-creepy asteroid even creepier. During its closest approach, the creepy asteroid was about 300,000 miles from Earth, or 1.3 times the average distance between Earth and the moon . So, it didn't pose a threat to our planet. It was discovered by astronomers at Hawaii's Pan-STARRS observatory only three weeks before the flyby, and it was given the official designation "2015 TB145." But no one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images.

articles.title: The moon, Mars, and Jupiter shine in the heart of the Lion overnight on Nov. 1-2
articles.excerpt: The waning moon shines with Jupiter, Mars and the brilliant star Regulus in the eastern sky overnight Nov. 1-2.
articles.body: The moon dives towards the glowing heart of the constellation Leo for a spectacular rendezvous with Mars and Jupiter overnight on Nov. 1-2, as the glittering stars of the Beehive Cluster shine nearby. Here's what you need to know. Look to the eastern horizon an hour after midnight to see the 45%-lit waning moon shining less than 5 degrees from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length to the night sky. Jupiter's bright light will gleam just below the red planet, with the bright star Regulus lining up beyond to form a dazzling procession leading back to the horizon. The stars of the Beehive Cluster (M44) can be found twinkling 10 degrees from the unlit side of the lunar disk around this time, in the middle of the constellation Cancer .

articles.title: Betelgeuse is haunted by a cosmic poltergeist tormenting the doomed star's atmosphere
articles.excerpt: Radio images show the supergiant's atmosphere recovering from its dramatic dimming, while a companion plows through its outer layers.
articles.body: Something spooky is stirring in the shadows of the infamous star Betelgeuse, a cosmic poltergeist that is disrupting the atmosphere of the red supergiant. New radio observations have shown Betelgeuse's smaller stellar companion, Siwarha (not Betelguese Betelguese, unfortunately), cutting through the supergiant's extended atmosphere and leaving a wake in its path, like a jet boat slicing through a lake.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
